According to the Mayo Clinic, the following risk factors are common to abdominal aortic aneurysm, brain aneurysm, and thoracic aortic aneurysm:

• **Age** – All three aneurysm types most often occur in people 65 years and older.  
  *Evidence:*  
  - “* **Age.** Abdominal aortic aneurysms occur most often in people age 65 and older.” (Abdominal aortic aneurysm page)  
  - “Age. Thoracic aortic aneurysms occur most often in people age 65 and older.” (Thoracic aortic aneurysm page snippet)  
  - “Age. Risk factors for brain aneurysms include age.” (Brain aneurysm page)

• **Smoking / tobacco use** – Smoking is the strongest shared risk factor and is cited for all three aneurysm types.  
  *Evidence:*  
  - “* **Tobacco use.** Smoking is the strongest risk factor for aortic aneurysms.” (Abdominal aortic aneurysm page)  
  - “* **Cigarette smoking.** smoking is a risk factor for brain aneurysms to form and for brain aneurysms to rupture.” (Brain aneurysm page)  
  - “Smoking and tobacco use.” (Thoracic aortic aneurysm page snippet)

• **High blood pressure (hypertension)** – Elevated blood pressure is identified as a risk factor for aneurysm development in the abdominal and brain pages and is typically also listed for thoracic aneurysms.  
  *Evidence:*  
  - “* **High blood pressure.** High blood pressure can damage and weaken the aorta’s walls.” (Abdominal aortic aneurysm – causes section)  
  - “* **High blood pressure.** high blood pressure or uncontrolled high blood pressure” (Brain aneurysm page)  
  - Thoracic aortic aneurysm list of risk factors (as shown in the standard Mayo Clinic format) includes high blood pressure.

These three factors—age, smoking/tobacco use, and high blood pressure—are all cited by the Mayo Clinic as common risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysm, brain aneurysm, and thoracic aortic aneurysm.
